patterns.signal: Addressables Analyze or a memory snapshot shows the same texture twice, once per group whose prefabs use it
patterns.why: Make shared textures, materials, shaders and atlases addressable in their own group so bundles reference one copy instead of each implicitly embedding it. Costs an extra bundle to load first.

patterns.signal: You release most enemies from a large Pack Together group, but memory barely drops while one is still in use
patterns.why: A bundle unloads only when its whole reference count hits zero, so group what loads and unloads together (per level, per feature). Too many tiny groups add bundle overhead and catalog size.

patterns.signal: `LoadAssetAsync` or `InstantiateAsync` calls are scattered around and memory grows with every level visited
patterns.use: Owner pairs every load with Release
patterns.why: Addressables is reference counted: one clear owner holds the handle and calls `Release` or `ReleaseInstance` on a lifecycle event. Missed releases leak; double releases unload content still in use.

patterns.signal: Code calls `Resources.Load("Prefabs/Boss")` and startup gets slower as the project grows
patterns.why: Resources ships everything in the folder, builds a startup index and only frees via the global `UnloadUnusedAssets`; string paths break on rename. Keep Resources for a few tiny bootstrap objects at most.

patterns.signal: Opening the main menu loads a 16 MB atlas because it shows one shop icon
patterns.use: Atlas by usage, not by folder
patterns.why: Any sprite pulls in its whole atlas texture, so pack per screen or feature plus one shared atlas for common icons. Finer atlases mean slightly more draw calls across screens.

patterns.signal: Texture memory on Android is several times the expected size; textures show RGBA32 or an unsupported format
patterns.why: ASTC on modern mobile, BC on desktop and consoles stay compressed in VRAM: a 2048 texture drops from 16 MB to about 1.8 MB at ASTC 6x6. Unsupported formats decompress at load and erase the gain.

patterns.signal: A UI texture drawn only by an `Image` has Read/Write and mipmaps enabled
patterns.why: Read/Write keeps a CPU copy (about double memory) and mips add about 33% that screen-space UI never samples. Keep Read/Write only when code reads pixels.

patterns.signal: Frame hitches on every screen change, and the profiler shows `Resources.UnloadUnusedAssets` each time
patterns.use: Unload only at natural pause points
patterns.why: It walks the whole object graph on the main thread, and non-additive scene loads already call it. Run it behind loading screens; rely on Addressables releases for steady-state memory.

patterns.signal: Producers want to ship new levels or events without a store update
patterns.use: Remote groups with a content catalog
patterns.why: Addressables remote groups on a CDN plus an updatable catalog let you swap content after release. Code changes still need a binary, and you take on hosting, cache and version compatibility.

patterns.signal: An imported Blender model looks right but its root shows Rotation X -90 and Scale 100
patterns.use: Bake axis and units at export
patterns.why: Apply transforms and set exporter axis and units, or use Bake Axis Conversion, so roots arrive at Rotation 0, Scale 1 in metres. Otherwise code that resets rotation or scale undoes the conversion.

patterns.signal: A wiki lists import rules, yet new textures keep arriving at 4096 with the wrong compression
patterns.why: Runs on every import on every machine: silently clamp size, set sRGB and platform overrides, and log import errors for what cannot be fixed. Bump `GetVersion()` when rules change to reimport.

patterns.signal: Each new asset in a folder needs the same starting importer settings
patterns.why: Default presets set importer values on first import with no code. They never touch assets already in the project, so pair them with a postprocessor or validator for enforcement.

patterns.signal: Assets imported before a rule existed, or changed by hand in the Inspector, still break the budget
patterns.why: Walk `Assets/Art`, check every importer and mesh against budgets and naming, print one line per violation and exit non-zero. Catches what import hooks never re-run on; costs CI Editor time.

patterns.signal: Every art review turns into a debate about whether this prop's triangle count is acceptable
patterns.why: Agree triangles, bones, draw calls, texture size and format per class (hero, crowd, background) from device profiling, stored in one asset both people and tools read. Needs an owner to revisit it.

patterns.signal: Metallic, occlusion and smoothness ship as separate textures, or a packed mask shades too dark and rough
patterns.why: One texture, one sample, one set of import settings. Masks are data, so import linear with a format that keeps channels independent (BC7, ASTC); normal maps stay separate.

patterns.signal: Some props look crisp and others blurry in the same frame, and texture sizes are chosen per asset
patterns.why: Pick pixels per metre per asset class: a 2 m crate at 512 px/m gets 1024 px. Consistent look and predictable memory; halving density quarters memory, small objects share atlases.

patterns.signal: Every FBX creates its own materials and artists ask for a new shader per asset
patterns.why: Engineers own a few master shaders with exposed properties; artists make materials and variants. Keeps keyword variants and SRP Batcher groups under control at the cost of a request queue.

patterns.signal: LOD Groups are set up by hand inconsistently and tools cannot tell meshes from textures
patterns.why: Prefixes like `SM_`, `SK_`, `T_` and suffixes `_N`, `_M`, `_LOD0` let the importer build LOD Groups and let tools pick rules. Only works if the scheme is short and checked automatically.

patterns.signal: A crowd of creatures or props uses a Humanoid rig though no clips are shared between skeletons
patterns.why: Generic plays curves on existing bones and is cheaper per character. Humanoid buys retargeting and humanoid IK; pay for it only where clips are shared across proportions.

patterns.signal: A fix made directly to an exported PNG or FBX disappears after the next export
patterns.use: Single source of truth in DCC files
patterns.why: Version the `.blend`, `.spp` or `.psd` (LFS or art repo) and regenerate exports from it. Nobody hand-edits exported files; costs storage for large sources.

patterns.signal: A new validation rule would turn hundreds of existing assets red on day one
patterns.why: Ship the rule as a warning with a published violation list, let art clear the backlog, then flip to an error. A rule that blocks everyone at once gets disabled within the week.

patterns.signal: Optimization decisions are based on Play Mode timings in the Editor profiler
patterns.use: Profile a development build on device
patterns.why: Editor numbers include EditorLoop, a desktop CPU and GPU, and Mono JIT. Use Development Build plus Autoconnect Profiler on the target device, without Script Debugging, which adds its own cost.

patterns.signal: Timeline shows the main thread finishing early, then waiting in `Gfx.WaitForPresentOnGfxThread`
patterns.why: Script optimization will not move the frame. Lower render resolution as a test, then reduce fill rate, overdraw, post-processing or shader cost, using platform GPU tools for per-pass timings.

patterns.signal: `Update` of a system costs 6 ms and you cannot tell which part, and Deep Profiling inflates call-heavy code
patterns.why: Markers cost almost nothing when not recording and compile out of release builds, so leave them in. Use Deep Profiling only briefly to locate a region, never for numbers.

patterns.signal: Someone claims a speedup from comparing one spiky frame before and after a change
patterns.why: Compare medians and worst frames over many frames of two captures on device. Single frames are noise; insist on a before and after capture for every claimed optimization.

patterns.signal: Memory stays 300 MB higher after returning from a level to the main menu
patterns.why: Snapshot before the level and after returning, then diff: leaked objects appear with the reference chain pinning them, such as a static list or event. Snapshots are large and pause the game.

patterns.signal: The Profiler says rendering is the cost and draw calls are higher than expected
patterns.why: Steps through every draw and states why consecutive draws did not batch (different material, shader keywords, lightmap). Works on a connected development build, not only the Editor.

patterns.signal: The game holds 60 fps for a few minutes on a phone, then settles near 40 with the same content
patterns.why: Run 15-30 minute tests on mid-range devices and budget about 65-70% of the frame; cap at 30 fps or scale quality, via Adaptive Performance where supported.

patterns.signal: A hot loop updates thousands of positions, projectiles or mesh vertices on the main thread
patterns.why: `IJobParallelFor` over `NativeArray` runs on worker threads and Burst vectorizes it, often 10x or more. Needs blittable data, no managed objects, and explicit disposal of native containers.

patterns.signal: Code calls `handle.Complete()` on the line right after `Schedule()`
patterns.why: Immediate completion makes the main thread wait for the job, removing most parallelism. Schedule as early as possible, do other work, complete only when results are needed.

patterns.signal: Hierarchy sorted by GC Alloc shows steady kilobytes per frame and periodic GC spikes
patterns.why: Cache arrays and strings, avoid LINQ and boxing in hot paths, use non-allocating API variants. Even incremental GC eventually spikes; allocation at load time is fine.

patterns.signal: Hundreds of projectiles or effects are instantiated and destroyed every second
patterns.why: Reuse deactivated instances instead of Instantiate/Destroy, removing allocation and setup cost. Pools hold memory at peak size and need careful state reset on reuse.

patterns.signal: The design calls for tens of thousands of similar simulated units and GameObject overhead dominates
patterns.why: Archetype chunks give tightly packed iteration with jobs and Burst. Costs a different programming model and tooling; most games are better served by Jobs + Burst on hot spots.

patterns.signal: A tool writes `((Door)target).locked = true` and the change is not undoable and vanishes on reload
patterns.why: `SerializedProperty` edits give undo, multi-object editing, prefab override tracking and dirtying for free. Remember `ApplyModifiedProperties()` after changes.

patterns.signal: A button must mutate a component directly, such as rebuilding a list from child Transforms
patterns.why: Record before the change (also marks dirty), then `PrefabUtility.RecordPrefabInstancePropertyModifications` for prefab instances. `EditorUtility.SetDirty` alone loses undo and overrides.

patterns.signal: The same min/max or ID-picker field appears on many components and each draws it differently
patterns.why: Write the drawer once and every field tagged with the attribute renders it in any inspector. Scope is one field; use a custom editor for whole-component layout or buttons.

patterns.signal: Designers need buttons, validation hints or grouped fields on one component's inspector
patterns.why: `[CustomEditor]` with `CreateInspectorGUI` builds a retained tree; `PropertyField` keeps default drawing and binding. IMGUI remains in legacy code but redraws every repaint.

patterns.signal: A designer repeats a multi-step workflow across many assets or scene objects by hand
patterns.why: A dockable panel built in `CreateGUI` can hold state, lists and batch operations. Costs ongoing maintenance, so build it where the repeated time clearly exceeds that.

patterns.signal: An occasional one-shot action (validate spawns, rebuild atlas) lives in a doc as manual steps
patterns.why: A static `[MenuItem]` gives a discoverable entry, and a validate method greys it out when not applicable. The same static method can be the batch-mode entry point.

patterns.signal: The Editor runs fine but the player build fails with `UnityEditor could not be found`
patterns.why: Put editor code in an asmdef whose platforms include only Editor, referencing the runtime asmdef. Inside an asmdef folder the special `Editor` folder rule no longer applies.

patterns.signal: A one-line change to an editor window triggers a 25 second recompile of all gameplay code
patterns.why: Only the changed assembly and its dependents recompile. Costs explicit references: asmdef code cannot see `Assembly-CSharp`, so dependencies must get asmdefs too.

patterns.signal: Import rules, scene lists or enemy stats are hard-coded constants inside tool code
patterns.why: Code holds behaviour, a `[CreateAssetMenu]` asset holds the knobs designers own, and changes are diffable text. Tools must handle the asset being missing or edited mid-session.

patterns.signal: A CI job must bake, validate or build without anyone clicking in the Editor
patterns.why: Run a static method with `-batchmode -quit -logFile -` and call `EditorApplication.Exit(1)` on failure. No dialogs in batch mode, and cache `Library` to avoid long cold imports.

patterns.signal: A runtime class needs a small editor-only hook such as an `OnValidate` that calls `AssetDatabase`
patterns.why: Keeps the hook out of the player without a separate assembly. Each block is a place where Editor and player diverge, so keep them tiny and never around serialized fields.

patterns.signal: Missing scripts and broken references are only found when someone happens to open a scene
patterns.why: One validator for missing scripts, broken references and import rules, runnable from a menu and `-executeMethod`. Becomes the verification step for humans, CI and agents.

patterns.signal: A save or JSON system works in the Editor but IL2CPP builds throw `MissingMethodException` or load default fields
patterns.why: The linker strips types reached only by reflection. Preserve the specific assemblies or types; disabling stripping or `preserve="all"` everywhere gives back the size you wanted to save.

patterns.signal: Daily builds use Mono and a release candidate crashes in a way nobody saw before
patterns.why: Mono for fast iteration is fine, but stripping and AOT bugs only show in IL2CPP players. Build and smoke-test IL2CPP regularly; it costs minutes per build.

patterns.signal: A dependency uses `System.Reflection.Emit` or generates code at runtime
patterns.why: IL2CPP compiles ahead of time, so runtime code generation fails on iOS, WebGL and consoles. Choose source-generated or AOT-compatible serializers and DI instead.

patterns.signal: Game rules live inside a MonoBehaviour, so testing them requires a scene and frames
patterns.why: Move logic into a plain C# class the MonoBehaviour delegates to; test it in fast EditMode tests. The thin component stays untested or covered by a few PlayMode tests.

patterns.signal: You need to check a combo multiplier or damage formula across dozens of input cases
patterns.why: Pure-logic NUnit tests run in milliseconds without Play Mode, so many cases stay cheap. They cannot catch engine-loop, physics or platform behaviour.

patterns.signal: A behaviour depends on `Awake`, `Update`, physics or coroutines advancing over frames
patterns.why: `IEnumerator` tests yield frames so the engine loop runs. Slower, often seconds each, so keep them for integration paths and run them in a built player for platform issues.

patterns.signal: A CI test step finishes quickly with no results file
patterns.why: The test runner exits on its own; `-quit` can end the process before tests run. Pass `-testResults` and fail the job on the exit code and the NUnit XML.

patterns.signal: Platform code in `#if UNITY_IOS` compiles fine for Android but fails on the first iOS build
patterns.why: Keep platform branches thin behind an interface with one small implementation each, and compile every target in CI. Code in an inactive `#if` is never compiled.

patterns.signal: A serialized field is wrapped in `#if UNITY_EDITOR` and players warn about layout or lose data
patterns.why: Editor and player must agree on serialized layout. Move editor-only data into assets the player never loads instead of conditionally compiling fields.

patterns.signal: Release builds are made by hand from someone's Editor and settings differ between machines
patterns.why: `BuildPipeline.BuildPlayer` from a batch method plus versioned Build Profiles makes builds reproducible, and the `BuildReport` gives result and size. Requires CI licence setup.

patterns.signal: The player size jumps after a content change and nobody knows which assets caused it
patterns.why: The per-file breakdown shows which assets and Resources content landed in the build; diff it between builds to catch duplicates and stray references before release.

patterns.signal: Each CI run spends most of its time reimporting the whole project
patterns.why: A warm `Library` turns cold imports of tens of minutes into short incremental ones. Key the cache by platform and Unity version; a stale cache can hide import bugs, so purge occasionally.

patterns.signal: After a rename, prefabs show missing scripts and the diff shows the old `.meta` deleted and a new one added
patterns.use: Rename and move inside the Editor
patterns.why: Unity references by GUID in the `.meta`; renaming in the Editor or `AssetDatabase.MoveAsset` keeps it. Shell or IDE renames without the meta generate a new GUID.

patterns.signal: References break on a teammate's machine but not yours, and an asset was committed without its `.meta`
patterns.why: Fail on any asset without a `.meta` or meta without an asset, and flag changed GUIDs. Cheap to run and catches most reference breakage before merge.

patterns.signal: A text merge of two scene edits succeeds but the scene loads with duplicate fileID errors
patterns.why: Smart Merge parses both sides as objects and merges by fileID and property. Wire it in `.gitattributes` and git config; true conflicts on the same object still need a human.

patterns.signal: Several designers edit one 5,000-object scene and conflict daily
patterns.why: Split content so people rarely touch the same file; no merge tool fixes concurrent edits of one object. Costs load orchestration and cross-scene reference management.

patterns.signal: Clones are huge because every revision of large PSDs and FBXs stays in Git history
patterns.why: LFS stores binaries on a separate server with pointers in Git; `git lfs lock` stops concurrent edits of unmergeable files. Locking only works if everyone checks locks.

patterns.signal: An art-heavy studio keeps losing work when two non-technical artists edit the same file
patterns.why: Unity Version Control or Perforce handle large binaries natively and enforce exclusive checkout with artist-friendly clients. Code-heavy Git teams may find LFS plus locks enough.

patterns.signal: Scene and prefab diffs are unreadable binary blobs in review
patterns.why: With Force Text and Visible Meta Files, assets become reviewable YAML that Smart Merge can handle. Text is still not safe to hand-edit: fileIDs and overrides must stay consistent.

patterns.signal: `git status` shows `Library/`, `Temp/` or `UserSettings/` changes, or packages differ between machines
patterns.use: Commit only the source of truth
patterns.why: Commit `Assets` with metas, `ProjectSettings`, `Packages/manifest.json` and `packages-lock.json`; ignore regenerable folders. The lock file makes package versions identical everywhere.

patterns.signal: An agent is asked to add a component to 120 prefabs and starts editing `.prefab` YAML
patterns.why: Have the agent write C# using `PrefabUtility`, `SerializedObject` and `AssetDatabase`, run in batch mode or a live Editor. Hand-written YAML risks invented fileIDs and unwired components.

patterns.signal: An agent reports a task done but never opened the project or read the console
patterns.use: Verify in a live Editor loop
patterns.why: Connect via MCP or the Unity CLI to check console errors, query the hierarchy and run EditMode tests and the validator. Success counts only when those pass.

patterns.signal: Agents keep creating `.meta` files, renaming with shell commands or reaching for `Resources.Load`
patterns.why: State in project instructions: no YAML or meta edits, move assets via the Editor, the loading strategy, and run tests after changes. Rules reduce mistakes but still need diff review.

patterns.signal: An agent diff contains large YAML changes in scenes the task never mentioned, or changed GUIDs
patterns.use: Reject and redo through the Editor
patterns.why: Unrelated scene churn and GUID changes signal hand-edited or regenerated assets. Revert and redo the change through Editor APIs rather than patching the YAML.
